video_title: Why Did The Jaylen Brown Trade Happen Now? + Lakers' New Big 3 vs Luka

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst on the responsibility of reporting team thinking
quotes.excerpt: when we say what teams are thinking, we have to be grownups and not destroy the messenger.
quotes.quote: When we say what teams are thinking, sometimes we're going to say what our opinion is. But when we say what teams are thinking, we have to be grownups and not destroy the messenger.

quotes.speaker: Vince Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Goodwill on the lack of logic in the Jaylen Brown trade
quotes.excerpt: Wait, he got traded to where? For who? Like it didn't make sense, right?
quotes.quote: I was recording a podcast with Carmelo Anthony in Brooklyn yesterday. When it came through, it was, 'Wait, he got traded to where? For who?' Like it didn't make sense, right? And I won't say it still doesn't make sense now, but when you add up some of the things, and it's hard to add up these things and for it to make sense to people: A, the Celtics have won a grand total of one first-round playoff series in the last two years. That is point one. Point two, Jaylen Brown and Jason Tatum are increasingly getting more expensive as time goes on, so you have to operate with some prudence in how you are building this team.

quotes.speaker: Vince Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Goodwill on the Celtics' lack of faith in Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: the Celtics clearly did not believe that was sustainable in a different environment come this season.
quotes.quote: Jaylen Brown had a fantastic season on paper last year, and the Celtics clearly did not believe that was sustainable in a different environment come this season. And they didn't believe that Jaylen Brown would be able to slide back into a supporting role, or if he would want to slide back into a supporting role, assuming Jason Tatum is all the way back into himself. It's a million things, right?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst on the league's valuation of Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: the league believes he's not a $57 million player. And that is asking for a lot of comprehension.
quotes.quote: I don't believe that the league doesn't think Jaylen Brown is a very good player. What I think is the league believes he's not a $57 million player. And that is asking for a lot of comprehension because there are people who not only are defending Jaylen Brown but defending the concept of the eye test versus analytics. Yes, there are all kinds of analytics, but in the era where there's essentially a hard salary cap, which is essentially what we have with the second apron, there's a lot more stress on you performing to your level of a player. Peyton Pritchard makes $7 million. Nobody in their right mind would ever say that Peyton Pritchard is a better basketball player than Jaylen Brown. In an era where the aprons mean everything and dollars define the efficiency of dollars defines your team, Peyton Pritchard is viewed as more efficient with his contract than Jaylen Brown is.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: MacMahon on the Celtics' decision to move on from Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: the Boston Celtics believed they needed to move on from Jaylen Brown.
quotes.quote: I had a primary decision-maker for another team in the league say, 'If you make $60 million, this is what you're worth in a trade.' If he made $40, every single team in the league would have been lining up for Jaylen, even with all of the other issues. Obviously, it reached a point where, for whatever reasons, the Boston Celtics believed they needed to move on from Jaylen Brown. I'm pretty sure they reached that point before they put him in an offer for Giannis Antetokounmpo. And then after that, they just had to find the best deal.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: MacMahon on the criticism of the Celtics' trade approach
quotes.excerpt: this is a classic case of the credit goes to the guy who scores, but they're not driving team success.
quotes.quote: This is a classic case of the credit goes to the guy who scores, but they're not driving team success. There's guys like this all over the league. The difference is he's not at $40 million, like a Brandon Ingram. He's at $60 million. And then it gets into the CBA and the cap rules and the apron, and he says, 'It's really hard to tie up that much money in your salary cap for one player unless they're truly generational, and he's not even close to that.'

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst on the Lakers' roster overhaul and Walker Kessler
quotes.excerpt: the Lakers yesterday, they went through a massive roster makeover because we're still dealing with the fallout.
quotes.quote: We just did the drive-by on the Lakers yesterday. They went through a massive roster makeover because we're still dealing with the fallout. Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, and Sandro Mamukelashvili. Pretty big turnover of the roster.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: MacMahon on Walker Kessler's role with the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: Walker Kessler is now a centerpiece of the Lakers. He's their number three guy for the long term.
quotes.quote: We can talk about kind of the ancillary pieces, but Walker Kessler is now a centerpiece of the Lakers. He's their number three guy for the long term, and whether you want to say they overpaid on salary and they overpaid on the price in terms of the picks, they've got their guy.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: MacMahon on the Jazz's valuation of Walker Kessler
quotes.excerpt: talking to people around the league, they thought the five years about $140 million on the table from the Jazz
quotes.quote: Talking to people around the league, they thought the five years about $140 million on the table from the Jazz was a very strong offer for Walker Kessler. The $500,000 a year wasn't going to prevent the Jazz from having gotten to $140 million. They felt like that was really strong value for Walker Kessler.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst on the future of the 'fun max' contract
quotes.excerpt: at some point here, Victor Wembanyama is going to get a max. Not going to be fun.
quotes.quote: There's no such thing in an apron era as the 'fun max'. And even paying a really good player the max, like, at some point here, Victor Wembanyama is going to get a max. Not going to be fun, because the Spurs will have to make other decisions.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst on Walker Kessler's required role for the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: you need Walker Kessler to be a grand slam. You need him to be a lob roll threat
quotes.quote: What they really need now is you need Walker Kessler to be a grand slam. You need him to be a lob roll threat that absolutely dunks a ball like crazy off Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves lobs. You need him to be able to stretch the floor a little bit, which he's been working on, and you need him to be a back-line defender who can be a killer defender, like all-defensive team candidate. That's what they need.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: MacMahon on the Lakers' defensive needs
quotes.excerpt: they need him to be a first-team all-defensive team who is a really good pick-and-roll partner
quotes.quote: No, like they need him to be a first-team all-defensive team who is a really good pick-and-roll partner with Luka and Austin.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst on the Lakers' draft asset management
quotes.excerpt: they entered the summer with three first-round picks they could trade. One of them was in the draft
quotes.quote: They entered the summer with three first-round picks they could trade. One of them was in the draft, which they used on Cameron Carr. He's there now, and then they traded the two others that they could have. In '32, they could trade a swap, but that they can't trade the pick itself.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst on the Lakers' lack of trade mechanisms
quotes.excerpt: they don't have any of those mechanisms right now. You look at, are they athletic enough?
quotes.quote: They don't have any of those mechanisms right now. You look at, are they athletic enough? That's the question. Are they athletic enough aside from Walker Kessler, who's clearly an above-average athlete playing center, but do you have enough athleticism around this ball club to make you a better perimeter defensive team?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst on the 76ers' roster construction around Maxey and Edgecombe
quotes.excerpt: this is a team that was largely and still it will be built around Maxey and Edgecombe
quotes.quote: So, obviously, this is a team that was largely and still it will be built around Maxey and Edgecombe and their speed. And so the question, Vince really is, how, how and where does Jaylen fit in playing with high-speed guards, Maxey and Edgecombe? Because that's the guy that, I mean, you know, if you have Embiid and, you know, he's getting the ball and Jaylen can educate him on his flopping and what not, that's a different conversation. You're going to play a certain way with Embiid, but you're probably going to have to fit in with the guards, and this is going to be a different style than Jaylen's played, because this is not the way the Celtics played.

quotes.speaker: Vince Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Goodwill on the defensive challenges for Jaylen Brown in Philadelphia
quotes.excerpt: defensively, because he won't have so much offensive responsibility because you have in theory, in theory Joel Embiid
quotes.quote: No, and also defensively, because he won't have so much offensive responsibility because you have in theory, in theory Joel Embiid, which always sounds like a good idea, and then reality happens. He's he's going to have to be a better defender. Like I saw some metrics and stuff and some numbers that said he was a below-average defender this year, and I think that he has the bones of being a well above-average defender.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst on the 76ers' salary cap situation
quotes.excerpt: the 76ers have 88% of their cap tied in Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and now Jaylen Brown.
quotes.quote: The 76ers have 88% of their cap tied in Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and now Jaylen Brown. And once again, I don't know what we're going to see out of Joel Embiid. Like I was, Philadelphia 76ers fans get mad at me, but when I saw them lose game one of their series, I knew they were cooked against the Knicks. When they went home on Mother's Day weekend, and it sticks out with me, your arena got taken over and you got beaten by 30 in every game. And that was basically with a running clock. I don't know how Jaylen Brown changes all of that, especially if the Celtics have graded him out to be so poor or whatever it was in so many different areas.

quotes.speaker: Vince Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Goodwill on the reality of NBA franchise player contracts
quotes.excerpt: every franchise is on the clock that has a franchise player locked under contract.
quotes.quote: I think we need to introduce all of the listeners, viewers to a unfortunate reality about this NBA that we're in. Every franchise is on the clock that has a franchise player locked under contract. It's not it's fun that Kawhi gets traded and Giannis gets traded or Jaylen Brown gets traded and everything else. You can be as great as you want to be. You are one bad 12 to 18 months stint away from that being your franchise and that being your franchise player. The bad side about how these things work, these contracts are not forever anymore. The days of the seven-year max or the six-year max, that doesn't happen. So as soon as you sign your deal, you're going to be up for an extension in two years. And in those two years, once again going back to it, if you are not going to resign with your team, you're going to be traded. If you don't want to resign with your team, they're going to trade you. Like this is what this is, so it's not specific to Luka that the Lakers were on the clock. Go look around at every superstar worth his salt in the NBA right now. Every team is on the clock.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst on the Pistons' acquisition of John Collins
quotes.excerpt: they lost Tobias Harris who resigned for the mid-level. Now maybe Tobias would not have resigned
quotes.quote: They lost Tobias Harris who resigned for the mid-level. Now maybe Tobias would not have resigned for the mid-level for the Pistons, and I don't know I want to assume that. But Tobias goes for the mid-level, you replace him with John Collins. Um, you know, he's more of a lob threat, I agree, than Tobias is, so maybe with Cade Cunningham, but like they didn't they held on to their cap space and their expiring contract in the middle of the season at the trade deadline when it was clear that they could have used some offensive help. Then they get into the summer and they resign Kevin Huerter for $9 million a year, and I'm happy for Kevin Huerter. But Landry Shamet got $6 million a year and shot 10% more and was a playoff contributor. Huerter got $9 million a year. They trade for Isaiah Joe, excellent trade, high, nice value, okay, but he's a backup. And I mean, you know, he's a guy they drafted and developed, which was, you know, I I know Jim Dolan's had a couple of mandates, which is one of which is not we're going we're not going to the second apron, but one of his other big mandates has been we got to draft and develop guys. And this is a guy they drafted and developed. Hey, I mean, he they they used him at times in the playoffs. Like he got playoff minutes. Anyway, and then they did a little thing called known as trading for Jaylen Brown. Okay. So, let's take a look at their roster right now.

quotes.speaker: Vince Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Goodwill on the Pistons' roster construction and Norm Powell
quotes.excerpt: Norm Powell would have filled a glaring need for the Pistons as that second score
quotes.quote: For example, Norm Powell would have filled a glaring need for the Pistons as that second score, you know, a guy who can create, a shooter alongside Cade Cunningham. Um, but Norm Powell decided that he would rather get more money in Chicago and more shots in Chicago than come to Detroit. Like Norm Powell, if they'd have signed Norm Powell, I'd be sitting here saying, 'Hey man, that's a really, really great fit for Detroit. He's not a superstar, but he's an All-Star who fits.' But they I like I don't know, can you trade for Tyler Herro? Like can you pull off something in the trade market with the flexibility and the picks that you have? They've got to find something because bringing back a team that feels like it hit their head on the ceiling in the second round last year, after barely getting out of the first round, that that's a tough look, man.
